title: The Muscle Proposes, the Nerve Disposes

scenes.tts: A newborn mouse that lacks the muscle kinase Musk cannot breathe. Its motor axons reach the diaphragm. So why does no junction form?
scenes.caption: A newborn mouse that lacks the muscle kinase MuSK cannot breathe. Its motor axons reach the diaphragm. So why does no junction form?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Muscle Proposes, the Nerve Disposes. A newborn mouse outline; a motor axon reaches a muscle fibre and stops, with no junction drawn. A question mark at the contact.
scenes.narration: A newborn mouse that lacks the muscle kinase MuSK cannot breathe. Its motor axons reach the diaphragm. So why does no junction form?

scenes.tts: A synapse is not built whenever an axon touches a target.
scenes.visual: The axon tip rests on the fibre; the contact stays plain. On-screen text: touching is not a synapse.
scenes.narration: A synapse is not built whenever an axon touches a target.

scenes.tts: At a mature junction, the acetylcholine receptors are packed under the nerve ending. Along the rest of the fibre, they are sparse.
scenes.visual: One long muscle fibre with receptors as small dots: a dense patch under one nerve terminal, scattered dots elsewhere.
scenes.narration: At a mature junction, the acetylcholine receptors are packed under the nerve ending. Along the rest of the fibre, they are sparse.

scenes.tts: So building a junction is a sorting problem. Where do the receptors go, and who tells them?
scenes.visual: The dots spread evenly along the fibre, then gather under the terminal. On-screen question: where do they go, and who tells them?
scenes.narration: So building a junction is a sorting problem. Where do the receptors go, and who tells them?

scenes.tts: The first clue came from frog muscle, in nineteen seventy-eight. Fibres and nerve terminals were made to degenerate.
scenes.caption: The first clue came from frog muscle, in 1978. Fibres and nerve terminals were made to degenerate.
scenes.visual: Date card: 1978, Sanes, Marshall and McMahan. A frog muscle fibre and its terminal fade away.
scenes.narration: The first clue came from frog muscle, in 1978. Fibres and nerve terminals were made to degenerate.

scenes.tts: Empty sheaths of basal lamina were left. Regenerating axons returned to the old synaptic sites.
scenes.visual: An empty basal lamina sheath with a gold mark at the old synaptic site. A regenerating axon grows back to the gold mark.
scenes.narration: Empty sheaths of basal lamina were left. Regenerating axons returned to the old synaptic sites.

scenes.tts: The basal lamina remembered where the synapse had been.
scenes.visual: The gold mark pulses. Label: basal lamina, the matrix around each fibre.
scenes.narration: The basal lamina remembered where the synapse had been.

scenes.tts: McMahan's group searched the electric organ of the ray Torpedo. In nineteen eighty-seven they named the protein agrin.
scenes.caption: McMahan's group searched the electric organ of the ray Torpedo. In 1987 they named the protein agrin.
scenes.visual: A Torpedo ray outline; its electric organ is split into fractions, tested on cultured muscle cells that form receptor clusters. Date card: 1987, agrin.
scenes.narration: McMahan's group searched the electric organ of the ray Torpedo. In 1987 they named the protein agrin.

scenes.tts: Motor neurons send their own form of agrin into the basal lamina.
scenes.visual: Agrin drawn as a short strand leaving the terminal and settling in the basal lamina. Label: neural agrin.
scenes.narration: Motor neurons send their own form of agrin into the basal lamina.

scenes.tts: Mice lacking Musk, a muscle receptor tyrosine kinase, make no junctions. Agrin acts through a complex that contains Musk.
scenes.caption: Mice lacking MuSK, a muscle receptor tyrosine kinase, make no junctions. Agrin acts through a complex that contains MuSK.
scenes.visual: Cross-section of the junction: terminal, basal lamina, muscle membrane, inside of the fibre. MuSK appears in the membrane, labelled receptor tyrosine kinase. Inset: MuSK-null, no junction.
scenes.narration: Mice lacking MuSK, a muscle receptor tyrosine kinase, make no junctions. Agrin acts through a complex that contains MuSK.

scenes.tts: Yet Musk alone does not bind agrin. What kind of molecule would you look for?
scenes.caption: Yet MuSK alone does not bind agrin. What kind of molecule would you look for?
scenes.visual: Agrin approaches MuSK and does not attach. A dashed gap marked with a question mark beside MuSK.
scenes.narration: Yet MuSK alone does not bind agrin. What kind of molecule would you look for?

scenes.tts: A protein on the muscle surface that binds agrin and joins Musk. That protein is L R P four.
scenes.caption: A protein on the muscle surface that binds agrin and joins MuSK. That protein is Lrp4.
scenes.visual: Lrp4 fills the gap: a large membrane protein that binds agrin outside the cell and sits beside MuSK.
scenes.narration: A protein on the muscle surface that binds agrin and joins MuSK. That protein is Lrp4.

scenes.tts: Cells that are not muscle bind neural agrin once they are given L R P four.
scenes.caption: Cells that are not muscle bind neural agrin once they are given Lrp4.
scenes.visual: Non-muscle cells: plain cells do not hold agrin; cells given Lrp4 hold it. Label: 2008.
scenes.narration: Cells that are not muscle bind neural agrin once they are given Lrp4.

scenes.tts: Inside the muscle, Dok seven binds activated Musk and boosts it. Rapsin, a scaffold under the membrane, holds the receptors together.
scenes.caption: Inside the muscle, Dok7 binds activated MuSK and boosts it. Rapsyn, a scaffold under the membrane, holds the receptors together.
scenes.visual: Dok7 docks on MuSK inside the fibre; MuSK glows brighter. Rapsyn gathers beneath a group of receptors.
scenes.narration: Inside the muscle, Dok7 binds activated MuSK and boosts it. Rapsyn, a scaffold under the membrane, holds the receptors together.

scenes.tts: The chain runs: neural agrin, L R P four, Musk with Dok seven, rapsin, then clustered receptors.
scenes.caption: The chain runs: neural agrin, Lrp4, MuSK with Dok7, rapsyn, then clustered receptors.
scenes.visual: The whole chain on screen: neural agrin, Lrp4, MuSK with Dok7, rapsyn, clustered receptors.
scenes.narration: The chain runs: neural agrin, Lrp4, MuSK with Dok7, rapsyn, then clustered receptors.

scenes.tts: Remove Musk or Dok seven, and no junctions form. Without rapsin, receptors are made but never clustered.
scenes.caption: Remove MuSK or Dok7, and no junctions form. Without rapsyn, receptors are made but never clustered.
scenes.visual: Each link in turn is crossed out; small panels show no junction for MuSK and Dok7, and scattered unclustered receptors for rapsyn.
scenes.narration: Remove MuSK or Dok7, and no junctions form. Without rapsyn, receptors are made but never clustered.

scenes.tts: Remove agrin, and fewer, smaller clusters remain. Hold on to that odd result.
scenes.visual: The agrin link is crossed out; a few small clusters remain on the fibre. The panel is tagged with a bookmark icon.
scenes.narration: Remove agrin, and fewer, smaller clusters remain. Hold on to that odd result.

scenes.tts: Here is the idea for this lesson. The muscle proposes; the nerve disposes.
scenes.visual: Guiding-idea card: The muscle proposes; the nerve disposes.
scenes.narration: Here is the idea for this lesson. The muscle proposes; the nerve disposes.

scenes.tts: The muscle builds clusters with its own machinery. The nerve decides which stay.
scenes.visual: The fibre shows several clusters with no nerve present (as in embryos with no motor axons). A terminal is added; one cluster is highlighted.
scenes.narration: The muscle builds clusters with its own machinery. The nerve decides which stay.

scenes.tts: Agrin, held under the terminal, raises Musk activity there and protects those clusters. Acetylcholine disperses the rest.
scenes.caption: Agrin, held under the terminal, raises MuSK activity there and protects those clusters. Acetylcholine disperses the rest.
scenes.visual: Agrin as a fixed patch under the terminal; the cluster beneath it stays. Clusters elsewhere fade.
scenes.narration: Agrin, held under the terminal, raises MuSK activity there and protects those clusters. Acetylcholine disperses the rest.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: without Musk, the muscle cannot build clusters, so no junction forms. When it can build, the nerve decides which clusters stay.
scenes.visual: Closing card: no MuSK, nothing to build; the muscle builds clusters; the nerve decides which stay.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: without MuSK, the muscle cannot build clusters, so no junction forms. When it can build, the nerve decides which clusters stay.
scenes.caption: Takeaway: without MuSK, the muscle cannot build clusters, so no junction forms. When it can build, the nerve decides which clusters stay.
